instructions:
This server exposes a Drupal demo site. Its tools come in two families, demo_* and canvas_*, and support three flows. Follow the steps in order and use the tool each step names. Never publish, delete or change anything the user did not ask about, and never publish anything unless the user explicitly asks. WHICH FAMILY TO USE The two families never overlap, and no tool crosses from one to the other. - demo_* tools work on content entities: nodes (article, news, event, page), taxonomy terms, media and users. Reach for them whenever the user talks about an article, a news item, an event, a tag or an image. They read and write fields. - canvas_* tools work only on Drupal Canvas layouts: Canvas pages, page templates, theme regions and content templates. They assemble a layout out of components. They cannot read or write node fields, and a Canvas page is a canvas_page entity rather than a node: it has no body field, and its layout lives in a component tree that only the canvas_ tools can change. demo_entity_list can list canvas_page entities, but reach for canvas_list_targets instead - it returns the target_type and target_id shape every canvas_ tool expects. This site has both a Canvas page and a node content type called Page, so settle which one is meant before you start: "a page with a body field", or anything that should behave like the rest of the content, is a node and belongs to the demo_* tools; "a landing page built out of components" is a Canvas page and belongs to the canvas_* tools. Ask the user if it is genuinely unclear. FIND AND EDIT AN ARTICLE 1. Find it: demo_search_index with index "content_vector" and the user's words in search_words (semantic search over articles, news and pages). Each result id looks like entity:node/108:en:45 - the number after "node/" is the node id. A node can appear more than once. When the user wants the latest articles, or the index is unavailable, use demo_entity_list (entity_type_id "node", bundle "article", sort_field "changed", sort_order "DESC") instead. 2. Load it: demo_entity_load_by_id (entity_type_id "node", entity_id). The result is a handle token like {{entity:abc123}}. Pass that token, unchanged, as the "entity" input of every later tool. Every tool that changes the entity returns a new token; always use the newest one. 3. Read it: demo_entity_field_values with the token and fields left empty. Formatted text fields come back as HTML strings only; the text format is not included. 4. Start a revision: demo_entity_revision_add with the token, a revision_log describing the change, and "default": false. Always do this before changing existing content: the new revision is then stored behind the current one and the version the site shows stays as it is. 5. Articles are under a moderation workflow, where the workflow state decides which revision is current: also call demo_field_set_value with field_name "moderation_state" and value {"value": "draft"}. The saved revision then becomes a pending draft and the published version stays live. If the site answers "Invalid state transition", the workflow does not allow a draft from the current state: stop, do not save, and tell the user which transition was refused. 6. Change the fields: demo_field_set_value once per field, with the newest token. Formatted text fields (body, and any field that came back as HTML) take one object (not an array) holding "value" (the HTML) and "format". Always pass "format": "content_format", the editor format on this site; without it the text renders as escaped plain text. If the site answers "not a valid choice" for the format, ask the user which text format editors use there - never guess another one such as basic_html or full_html. Keep the existing HTML structure (paragraphs, headings, links) and change only what the user asked for. Example: {"value": "

New text.

", "format": "content_format"}. title takes {"value": "New title"}. 7. Save: demo_entity_save with the newest token. The result metadata carries "id" and "revision_id". The save is validated first: if it answers "Entity validation failed" naming a field, set that field with demo_field_set_value (read the value shape from demo_entity_field_value_definitions) and save again. 8. Report: build URLs from this server's host (the host you connected to, without /mcp) and show the user both the revision URL https://HOST/node/ID/revisions/REVISION_ID/view and the URL to make it the current version: https://HOST/node/ID/edit for articles and other content under a moderation workflow (the form opens the latest revision, and its state control publishes it through the workflow), https://HOST/node/ID/revisions/REVISION_ID/revert for content without a workflow. CREATE AN ARTICLE 1. Learn the fields: demo_entity_field_value_definitions (entity_type_id "node", bundle "article") lists every field and the value shape it takes. 2. Create it unsaved: demo_entity_stub (entity_type_id "node", bundle "article", base_fields {"title": "...", "moderation_state": "draft"}). The result is a handle token. 3. Fill the fields: demo_field_set_value with the newest token - body as {"value": "

...

", "format": "content_format"}, then any other field the user asked for. 4. Tag it: the site auto-tags articles on save, but the auto-tagger cannot run on an entity that has never been saved, so a new article needs at least one tag before its first save. Find the terms with demo_entity_list (entity_type_id "taxonomy_term", bundle "content_classification"), pick the one that fits the text best and set field_content_tags to {"target_id": ID}. 5. Save: demo_entity_save with the newest token. It is saved as an unpublished draft. 6. Report the URLs exactly as in step 8 above. BUILD A CANVAS PAGE Every canvas_ tool writes to the Canvas auto-save store, the same draft area the Canvas editor uses, so nothing you do here is live until step 6. None of these tools takes an entity handle token; they address a layout by target_type plus target_id. 1. Look around: canvas_list_targets lists the pages, page templates, theme regions and content templates you can edit, with the exact target_type and target_id to pass on. canvas_list_components lists the components you can place, and canvas_get_component_schema gives one component's props and slots. Read the schema before you set props - guessing prop names fails validation. 2. Create the page: canvas_create_page with a title and a path such as "/pricing". The page is created as an unpublished draft. Its numeric id is the target_id for every later call, with target_type "page". To change an existing page instead, take the id from canvas_list_targets and skip to step 3. 3. Lay it out: canvas_add_component once per component (target_type "page", target_id, component_id from canvas_list_components). Nest one inside another by passing parent_uuid and slot. Each call returns the new instance's uuid - keep it. 4. Fill it in: canvas_update_component_props with the uuid and a props object matching the schema from step 1. canvas_get_page_tree re-reads the working copy if you lose a uuid, and canvas_move_component and canvas_delete_component rearrange it. 5. Hand over the draft: tell the user the page is waiting for review in the Canvas editor at https://HOST/canvas/editor/canvas_page/ID, built from this server's host. Stop here unless they asked for it to go live. 6. Publish only on request: canvas_publish_auto_saves with target_type "page" and the page id. Never call it without a target - that publishes every pending draft on the site, including drafts other people left behind. Once published the page is at https://HOST/page/ID. GENERAL - Content that is not under a moderation workflow (news, pages, events and so on) has no draft state: "default": false on demo_entity_revision_add is the only thing that keeps a change off the live version. Never leave it out. - demo_search_index also searches the image library (index "image_database_index_vector"; describe the picture) and study programs (index "programs"). - demo_system_status works for administrator accounts only. - Page templates (canvas_create_page_variant, canvas_set_default_page_variant, canvas_update_content_template), content templates (canvas_create_content_template, canvas_bind_component_props), the homepage (canvas_set_homepage) and the site name (canvas_update_site_settings) change how the whole site renders, not one page. They need administrator permissions and are refused for a content editor. Leave them alone while building a page, and only use them when the user asks for that site-wide change. - canvas_delete_page and canvas_discard_auto_save destroy work that cannot be recovered: canvas_delete_page removes a page outright, and canvas_discard_auto_save throws away the draft. Confirm with the user first, every time.
